narratives.Description: Recut of #3917. The original body asked for the mechanism that resets the main checkout to origin/master. The bound arc established that identifying that actor is not achievable on the available evidence. This story ships the two buildable items the synthesis named: stop the unscoped `git worktree prune` on the evaluator-remove failure path, and close the documented fail-open at the write fence for destructive git, with a durable record that survives reflog prune.

narratives.Overview:
Do not build the original issue body. Original AC1 (identify the mechanism) and original AC4 (a gate run against a dirty tree leaves it byte-identical) are dropped: AC1 is unclosable, AC4 already holds and banking a test for it would prove nothing. Do not claim a root cause in the PR, CHANGELOG, or this brief.

Established by the arc (do not re-investigate): no non-test product code issues a checkout, reset, clean, restore, stash or pull; no post-checkout hook exists; the host kept no argv record for the incident window; the original lead (legacy-detect.ts:422) is dead.

Item 1: `removeEvaluatorWorktree` currently calls `git worktree prune` with no path, twice on the failure path. That operates on every registration and deletes pruned worktrees' administrative directories, including reflogs. Scope the cleanup to the worktree being removed, or drop the unscoped prune. Prove with a test that a second registered worktree survives a failed removal of the first.

Item 2: `content/contracts/path-write-fence.md` lists `git reset --hard` and `git checkout` as unrecognized mutators on a fail-open path, and states that nothing on the allow path is audited. Make tree-wide destructive git (`reset --hard`, `clean -f`, `checkout -f`/`switch -f`, `stash drop`/`clear`) recognized with a fail-closed disposition and a remediation line, always-on (not behind `shellDestForms: enforce`). Distinguish a command aimed at the project root from one aimed at a throwaway fixture via absolute out-of-root relocators only. Do not break Node-spawned `reset --hard` against temp fixtures.

Item 3: At that same boundary, append a durable JSONL record outside the repository (platform user-config dir) so the next occurrence names its actor even if reflogs are pruned.

Out of scope: restating original AC4 as new work; claiming a root cause; hunting the resetting process.

items.title: removeEvaluatorWorktree never runs unscoped `git worktree prune`; a second registered worktree survives a failed removal of the first

Tree-wide destructive git (`reset --hard`, `clean -f`, `checkout -f`/`switch -f`, `stash drop`/`clear`) is recognized at the Shell write fence and fail-closed when aimed at the project, with a remediation line
The same fence records a durable JSONL event outside the repository so a later occurrence names host, actor, command, project root, and disposition even if reflogs are gone
Absolute out-of-root git relocators (`-C` / `--git-dir` / `--work-tree` / `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE`) classify as fixtures and are allowed; relative or in-project relocators stay denied
Contract, fixtures README decision-code row, and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] record the recut: detection and a guard, no root cause

clauses.text: A test in which a second registered worktree survives a failed removal of the first, and removeEvaluatorWorktree never invokes unscoped git worktree prune
Destructive git aimed at the project root is recognized and denied fail-closed with a remediation line; an absolute out-of-root fixture relocator is allowed
A durable record of the command, actor, host, project root and disposition is written outside the repository so it survives reflog prune
PR, CHANGELOG and brief claim detection and a guard, not a root cause; original AC1 and AC4 are not restated as new work
